newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $0.50-trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $0.50-trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, but trade was expected to be extremely light before the Easter holiday weekend, livestock dealers said.
Weakness was expected from continued bearish fundamentals, including more than adequate hog supplies, heavy-weight hogs, they said.

Light demand from several packers who will close plants on Monday in observance of Easter also could pressure prices, the dealers said. Marketings were seen much lighter on Friday following heavy movement this week, the dealers said.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog receipts on Wednesday totaled 128,000 head, well above that day's estimate of 110,000, USDA statistics showed. Thursday's estimate was 110,000 head. Several dealers said Wednesday's rush of hog marketings were tied to pre-Easter movement, with producers aware that packer demand would be light on Monday.
Top prices at interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs at the plant could range $49.50 to mostly $50.00. Illinois top hog prices at the plant could range $50.00 to $50.50.
Indiana/Ohio top prices at the plant could range $49.00 to $50.00, dealers said.
